elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative clause states that “Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly permits termination “upon thirty (30) days' prior” notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly requires “written notice.”

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must refund prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: Commerce One is required to “refund to Corio any prepaid fees” following such termination.

elements.element: The refund must be pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: The refund covers prepaid fees “allocable to the period after the effective date of such termination,” which implements a pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: No operative provision grants Commerce One a mid-term convenience-termination right. Section 11.1 permits termination at expiration of a term, while Section 11.2 addresses termination for cause or insolvency.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative clause expressly grants Corio a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative clause specifies thirty (30) days' notice, not a notice period within the stated 60–90 day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee may not exceed three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no early-termination fee and expressly permits termination “without payment of any termination fee, penalty or other charge,” so the fee is below the cap.

elements.element: Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits either party, including Commerce One, to terminate at the expiration of the initial or a renewal term by giving notice of its intention to terminate.

elements.element: Vendor may exercise termination for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Commerce One's only no-cause termination mechanism is Section 11.1 termination at term expiration; its other termination rights require breach or insolvency.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' notice to terminate for convenience at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires only thirty (30) days' prior written notification, allowing Vendor to terminate at term end without the required 90-day minimum.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position. The fallback independently fails because it uses a 30-day Customer notice period rather than 60–90 days and retains Vendor's end-of-term termination right on only 30 days' notice rather than 90. The redline is not strictly minimal because it additionally grants partial termination and expressly eliminates every termination fee, penalty, or charge; neither addition is necessary to state the supplied preferred elements. It otherwise preserves the existing for-cause, insolvency, term, and renewal provisions without contradiction. Drafting quality is reduced because “in whole or in part” introduces partial-termination rights without specifying how partially terminated services, fees, or continuing obligations are treated.
